threads.body: [General] Run this exit advice when `receive` throws. The enter advice has already incremented the shared call depth, so skipping exit on a `JMSException` leaves the thread's depth nonzero and suppresses telemetry for later receives on that thread.

[General] Include exceptional exits here. `JMSConsumer.receive*` can throw a runtime JMS error after `enter()` increments the `MessageConsumer` call depth; without exit advice, that depth leaks and all subsequent receives on the thread are treated as nested.

[General] Include exceptional exits here. A runtime JMS error currently bypasses `AdviceScope.exit()`, leaving the shared call depth incremented and suppressing every later receive on the same thread.

[General] Run this exit advice when `receive` throws. Otherwise the newly incremented shared call depth is never decremented, permanently suppressing later receive telemetry on the same thread after a provider error.

[General] This exit advice does not run when `receive` throws, so the call depth incremented on entry is never decremented. The thread then treats every later `MessageConsumer.receive*` call as nested and suppresses its telemetry. Run the exit advice for exceptional returns as well; the nullable return value will keep span creation skipped while restoring the depth.

Checked the spec on this. Works for `CLIENT_ACKNOWLEDGE` and transacted sessions, but not for `AUTO_ACKNOWLEDGE` / `DUPS_OK_ACKNOWLEDGE` - there the provider has to "behave as if the unsuccessful call to receiveBody had not occurred", redelivering the message ahead of subsequent ones without setting `JMSRedelivered` or bumping `JMSXDeliveryCount`. After `receive()` the message is already consumed and acknowledged, so a failed `getBody(c)` just drops it. Same for `receiveBody(c, timeout)` and `receiveBodyNoWait(c)`.

We could put the session mode on the `JMSConsumer` in a VirtualField when JMSContext creates it, like `JmsSubscriptionNames` does for durable consumers, and only take that path for `CLIENT_ACKNOWLEDGE` and transacted. Worth doing, or leave `receiveBody` out with a comment?
If it can't be done reasonably then it is fine to omit it.

Left it out. Updated the javadoc in `ffbb623` so it gives the actual reason (the auto-ack redelivery rule) instead of the old one.

[Javaagent] This additive JMS 2.0 API support should not create a second overlapping javaagent project. The repository's compatibility-range convention says that optional APIs introduced in a higher subrange belong in an independently selected `InstrumentationModule` within the existing project, with separate Muzzle passes and `excludeInstrumentationName(...)` entries (`.github/agents/knowledge/gradle-conventions.md:39-57`); the Jedis 2.3 cluster module is a concrete example. Keeping this under `jms-1.1/javaagent` would also avoid the new implementation dependency back to that project and the reciprocal sibling test wiring while still allowing the `jms-2.0` instrumentation name.

[Javaagent] If startup throws after this increment—for example, a null `Message` makes `JavaxMessageAdapter.create` fail in its `VirtualField.get`—the enter-advice suppression keeps the application running but this shared `MessageProducer` call depth remains at 1. Every later classic or simplified send on the same thread is then treated as nested and emits no producer span. Decrement before rethrowing startup failures; a failed-send-then-valid-send regression test would protect the invariant.
